AIGenerationConfig.title: AIGenerationConfig

AnalysisAudit.description: What produced a result, so a past run can be reconstructed.
AnalysisAudit.title: AnalysisAudit

CaseAnalysisOverview.description: The latest per-case analysis in brief; the full result is GET /cases/{id}/analysis.
CaseAnalysisOverview.title: CaseAnalysisOverview

CaseCounts.description: What the queue's sidebar shows: every case, and how many are in each documents status.
CaseCounts.title: CaseCounts

CaseDocumentsStatus.description:
Rollup of every document under a case, worst-first: a single stuck
document outranks nine analyzed ones. Computed live from the documents
table on every read — never stored — since "stuck" is itself a
time-elapsed condition with no event that would keep a stored column
honest (see case_service.py).
CaseDocumentsStatus.title: CaseDocumentsStatus

CaseFindingReviews.description: Every review in a case, and the precision and recall they give: per document, across documents and for the case.
CaseFindingReviews.title: CaseFindingReviews

CaseListItem.description: One row of the case queue: only what the list shows, so it needs no extracted fields.

CaseListPage.description: One page of the case queue. `total` counts every case matching the search and status filter.
CaseListPage.title: CaseListPage

CaseNote.description:
A loan officer's note on a case, or on one of its documents (document_id). parent_id marks a
reply to an earlier note. Only its author can edit or delete it; edited_at shows it was edited.
A deleted note that has replies stays as a placeholder (deleted_at set, its text erased) so the
replies keep their place.
CaseNote.title: CaseNote

CaseRisk.description:
The case's risk level, rolled up from its documents' detection
findings — see case_risk.compute_case_risk for how it's scored. Only
"scored" carries a level; the other states say why there isn't one yet.
CaseRisk.title: CaseRisk

CaseSearchResult.description: Jump-to-case suggestions: the best matches (exact number first), and how many cases match in all.
CaseSearchResult.title: CaseSearchResult

CaseSummary.description:
documents_status, fulfilled_requirements and missing_requirements are all
computed live from the documents table on every read, never stored — see
case_service.py.
CaseSummary.title: CaseSummary

CheckAssessment.description:
AC5: the relevant check is marked Unable to Assess when its inputs
cannot be extracted or there isn't enough comparable content.
CheckAssessment.title: CheckAssessment

CheckMetrics.description:
One check's counts and rates. precision is correct / (correct + wrong): None when no finding of the check
was reviewed. recall is correct / (correct + missed): None when there is nothing it should have caught.
CheckMetrics.title: CheckMetrics

CompanyNameDiscrepancy.description: One company name, different from this document's, and every document that carries it.
CompanyNameDiscrepancy.title: CompanyNameDiscrepancy

CreateNoteRequest.description: A new note: on the whole case, on one of its documents, or a reply to an earlier note (parent_id).
CreateNoteRequest.title: CreateNoteRequest

DateAnomalyResult.description:
Response for GET /documents/{id}/detection/date-anomalies. Nothing is
persisted — a pure read/compute, like the spelling/layout/numerical
checks.
DateAnomalyResult.title: DateAnomalyResult

DetectionMetrics.description: Precision and recall per check across every reviewed case.
DetectionMetrics.title: DetectionMetrics

DocumentFieldInfo.description: A recognised injectable field (PDF text span, OCR text, or embedded image).

kind.description: 'text' or 'image'. image_manipulation targets embedded PDF images or pictorial regions on PNG/JPEG.
kind.title: Kind

source.description: How the field was recognised: 'pdf_text' or 'ocr'
source.title: Source

DocumentFieldInfo.title: DocumentFieldInfo

Event.description: One domain event. Carries ids only (Supabase holds the state), and is also the audit_events row.

ExtractedDate.description:
AC1/AC2: one date pulled out of the document's extracted fields,
labelled with a human-readable description.
ExtractedDate.title: ExtractedDate

FieldComparison.description: One document-vs-case comparison — AC4's "what caused the mismatch".
FieldComparison.title: FieldComparison

FindingReview.description:
An officer's verdict on one finding (kind "verdict": correct or wrong), or an issue the officer found that
no finding raised (kind "missed"). scope "document" is a finding on one document; "case" a cross-document
finding from the case analysis. check_name is the tool for a document finding, the category for a case one.
FindingReview.title: FindingReview

FontAnomalyV2.description: One deviation pattern, fact-only (no confidence scoring).
FontAnomalyV2.title: FontAnomalyV2

IdDocumentCoverage.description:
How many of the case's identified individuals (grouped the same way as
proof_of_address_coverage — by id_number, falling back to name) have a
complete id_document (front+back matched by id_number, or a
self-contained single capture) on file, out of how many identities have
been identified at all. total=0 means no id_document has been accepted
yet — see mapper.compute_id_document_identity_progress.
IdDocumentCoverage.title: IdDocumentCoverage

ImageIntegrityResult.description:
Both image checks on one document: SCRUM-64 and SCRUM-65. `report` comes
first and is written for a reader; the raw measurement-level results
follow unchanged for debugging.
ImageIntegrityResult.title: ImageIntegrityResult

indicator.description: Required for image_manipulation: resolution_mismatch, compression_mismatch, visible_boundary, scaling_anomaly, image_overlay, quality_mismatch.
indicator.title: Indicator

metadata.description: Required for metadata defects (author, creator, title, subject).
metadata.title: Metadata

new_text.description: Required for spelling, numerical, and text_overlay. Label prefixes are kept if you pass only the value.
new_text.title: New Text

scale_x.description: Optional scaling_anomaly horizontal factor. Values >1 spread wider. Default 1.85.
scale_x.title: Scale X

scale_y.description: Optional scaling_anomaly vertical factor. Values <1 compress shorter. Default 0.45.
scale_y.title: Scale Y

x.description: Required for misalignment (with y) — absolute x.
x.title: X

y.description: Required for misalignment (with x) — absolute y.
y.title: Y

defect_count.description: Total defects injected into this working document so far
defect_count.title: Defect Count

generated_filename.description: Output file in documents_generated/, safe to delete after you copy it out.
generated_filename.title: Generated Filename

LayoutAnomaly.description:
One affected area (same page and bbox), not one check.

`anomaly_type` is the strongest check: Indentation, Alignment, Margin,
or Spacing. Extra checks on the same area are `evidence.signals`, not
extra rows.     Neighbouring full-width flagged clauses set `local_pattern` and
`consecutive_run` on this finding; they need not share anomaly_type.
`detected` / `expected` / `deviation` hold the measurements on the
object. The JSON body keeps `summary` and a `checks` list
(check, detected, expected, difference) and leaves out the repeated
evidence dict. `bbox` / `text` are for highlighting.
LayoutAnomaly.title: LayoutAnomaly

LayoutAnomalyResult.description:
Response for GET /documents/{id}/detection/layout-anomalies.

Each of indentation / alignment / margin / spacing can be Unable to
Assess while the other families still return findings. Empty anomalies
with unable_to_assess=false means the checks ran and nothing exceeded
a threshold — not that the document is free of fraud.
LayoutAnomalyResult.title: LayoutAnomalyResult

LayoutElement.description:
Per-paragraph baseline used to form comparable groups. Headers are
not compared to body copy, so a centred company name is not an
Alignment anomaly just because the clauses under it are left-aligned.
LayoutElement.title: LayoutElement

MoveDocumentRequest.description: Reassigns a document to a different case — see routers/documents.py's move_document.
MoveDocumentRequest.title: MoveDocumentRequest

NumericalValidationResult.description:
Response for GET /documents/{id}/detection/numerical-validation.
Nothing is persisted — a pure read/compute, like the spelling and
layout checks.

Two independent Benford passes over transaction amounts (all amounts,
and amounts with likely bank fees excluded) are named benford /
benford_excluding_fees; both are None when the document type has no
transaction list to run them on.
NumericalValidationResult.title: NumericalValidationResult

ProofOfAddressCoverage.description:
How many of the case's identified individuals (one per accepted
id_document) currently have an address on file, out of how many there
are — see mapper.compute_identity_proof_of_address_progress.
total=0 means no ID document has been accepted yet, so there's nothing
to report coverage against (distinct from 0 covered out of >0 total).
ProofOfAddressCoverage.title: ProofOfAddressCoverage

RecommendationItem.description:
One thing a supporting document is requested for: a bank statement
transaction, or a line of a financial statement.
RecommendationItem.title: RecommendationItem

RegistryFinding.description: A numerical finding that also names the outside reference that said so.
RegistryFinding.title: RegistryFinding

ReportMissedIssueRequest.description: An issue the officer found that no finding raised, against the check that should have caught it.
ReportMissedIssueRequest.title: ReportMissedIssueRequest

RoutingStatus.description:
Routing decision made at the classification stage, independent of
whether the later Extraction stage subsequently succeeds or fails.
ACCEPTED means classification met the confidence threshold and was
routed to Analysis — it does not mean the document ultimately reached
ANALYZED status. Backed by the documents.routing_status column.
RoutingStatus.title: RoutingStatus

SetFindingVerdictRequest.description: Marks one finding correct or wrong; verdict null clears the officer's mark.
SetFindingVerdictRequest.title: SetFindingVerdictRequest

SetFindingVerdictsRequest.description: A whole group's review at once: every finding the officer looked at, each correct or wrong.
SetFindingVerdictsRequest.title: SetFindingVerdictsRequest

SpellingAnomaly.description:
One distinct unrecognised word: reported once however often it appears (a letterhead word
repeated on every page is one question, not one per page).
SpellingAnomaly.title: SpellingAnomaly

seconds_in_current_status.description: How long the document has sat in its current status
seconds_in_current_status.title: Seconds In Current Status

SupportingDocumentRecommendation.description:
A document the officer should request from the client, and why — see
supporting_documents.recommend_supporting_documents.
SupportingDocumentRecommendation.title: SupportingDocumentRecommendation

TamperingTolerances.description:
AC7 — what counts as normal variation. Calibrated against the 205 clean
documents in documents_generated and 260 injections of each SCRUM-65
indicator by the repo's own injection tool.
TamperingTolerances.title: TamperingTolerances

Tolerances.description:
AC6 — what counts as normal variation.

Defaults are deliberately loose. Scanning, photocopying, resizing and
ordinary PDF generation all shift these numbers around, and a check that
an officer learns to ignore is worse than no check, so each threshold is
set where an innocent explanation stops being plausible rather than
where a difference first becomes measurable.
Tolerances.title: Tolerances

UpdateCaseRequest.description:
A loan officer updating the case's own identifying details. Only
company_name is officer-editable today — status, submission_finalized
and greenlink_case_id are system-managed (see case_service.py /
case_repository.set_submission_finalized) and deliberately excluded
here so they can't be overwritten through this endpoint.
UpdateCaseRequest.title: UpdateCaseRequest

UpdateDocumentTypeRequest.description:
A loan officer's manual correction of a low-confidence document_type.
"unrecognised" is the "Other" catch-all — see extraction_prompts.
UpdateDocumentTypeRequest.title: UpdateDocumentTypeRequest

UpdateExtractedFieldsRequest.description:
A loan officer's manual correction of low-confidence extracted fields.
Replaces the full extracted_fields dict (not a per-field patch) since
the frontend always edits the complete set it was shown.
UpdateExtractedFieldsRequest.title: UpdateExtractedFieldsRequest

UpdateMissedIssueRequest.description: Corrects a reported missed issue: the check it's filed against, and its note. Where it sits never changes.
UpdateMissedIssueRequest.title: UpdateMissedIssueRequest

UpdateNoteRequest.description: A note's new text. Where the note sits (case, document, parent) never changes.
UpdateNoteRequest.title: UpdateNoteRequest

WaitingDocument.description:
A document the case's risk score counts that isn't scanned yet, and what it is waiting for: still being
processed, an officer's approval, its detection scan, or a retry after it failed. A rerun before these are
done can't produce a score.
WaitingDocument.title: WaitingDocument

delete.description:
Removes a case from the active queue, along with every document that
belongs to it. A following GET /cases or GET /cases/{id} no longer
returns it.

Only allowed once every one of the case's documents has reached a
terminal state (ANALYZED, FAILED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, APPROVED) — same
reasoning as delete_document: deleting out from under a document a
worker is still actively writing to (status, extracted fields) would
race the pipeline and orphan a document row mid-flight. Cancel the
in-flight document(s) first, or wait for them to finish.

Starts the per-case analysis (cross-document findings, risk outlook and
summary) in the background. Only once every approved document has been
scanned; poll GET .../analysis, or watch the case snapshot, for the result.

Whether each of the case's documents belongs to the case's company and
individuals, checked against the certificate of incumbency — see
case_match.py. Computed live on every call; nothing is written.
Every stored detection report for a case's documents, for one combined view.

get.description: Every review in the case, with precision and recall per document, across documents and for the case.

put.description:
Marks one finding correct or wrong, signed by the officer; a null verdict clears the mark. Any officer
can change a verdict; the latest one stands.

Saves one group's review in one request: the officer ticked the findings that are real (correct) and left
the rest (wrong). Every target is checked before anything is written, so a bad entry saves nothing.

delete.description: Removes a verdict or a missed issue (e.g. one reported by mistake).

patch.description:
Corrects a reported missed issue (its check or note), e.g. one filed against the wrong check. A verdict
on a finding is changed by reviewing the finding again, not here.

Saves a note signed by the officer making the request. Allowed on any document, approved and
rejected ones included: a note is stored on its own and never edits the document, so the
document's lock is untouched. Any officer can reply to a note (parent_id).

delete.description:
Deletes the officer's own note. Replies by anyone stay: a note with replies becomes a "This
note was deleted" placeholder above them (see notes_repository.delete_note).

patch.description: Replaces the text of the officer's own note and stamps edited_at. Its document is never touched.

get.description: Precision and recall per check across every reviewed case, with targets (the dashboard).

The single move applied to a batch, with each affected case resynced once.

get.description:
Single place to check what needs attention: stuck documents, documents
that exhausted retries (status=failed), and pipeline-level errors that
have no document row to attach to (e.g. a dequeued document whose row
vanished) — instead of having to know to filter for each separately.
AC4: surfaces documents stuck in uploaded/queued/processing past the threshold.

schema.title: Response List Stuck Documents Documents Monitoring Stuck Get

post.description:
Validates/stores/queues one or more files under one case_id in a single
request (AC1: returns as soon as they're queued, without waiting for
classification to complete). Each file is handled independently — one
bad file does not fail the rest of the batch.

delete.description: Removes a document from its case. Only once it is out of flight; cancel an in-flight one first.

post.description: Approves an analysed document after officer review, and starts detection.

Stops a QUEUED, PROCESSING or EXTRACTING document. The status write is a compare-and-swap, so
racing cancels or a finishing run can't both win; only then is the in-flight run interrupted.

get.description: What the content guard found at ingest, for the officer to see on the document page.
Scores the document's photographs, scans or image upload for traces of AI generation, with each indicator's value and contribution. A low score is not proof the image is genuine.

post.description:
Interrupts an in-flight detection run — the Detection panel's Cancel
action while a document reads "Scanning"/"Detecting". Only takes effect
at the graph's next await point (an Anthropic call already in flight
still completes) — see workers/detection.py. The cancellation is then
recorded the same way a crash is, so GET .../detection/report and
retry_document_detection below both already know how to handle it.

schema.title: Response Cancel Document Detection Documents  Document Id  Detection Cancel Post

get.description:
Whether this document belongs to its case's company and individuals —
the identity comparison used by fraud detection (see case_match.py). The check needs
every document in the case (the certificate of incumbency is only
trusted once other documents corroborate it), so this runs the whole
case's check and returns this document's entry. Read-only.
This document's company name against every other company document in its case.
Every labelled date in the extracted fields, and the inconsistent or suspicious ones (no file download).

The extracted facts against outside references chosen by document type: live ACRA, OneMap and HDB lookups, and published tables (CPF, GST, IRAS, bank identifiers, GIRO holidays). An unreachable registry is a skipped check, never a finding.
Font, size and embedding consistency across the document's text.
Both image checks in one call (the file is downloaded once), with a report written for a reader.

Compares the resolution and compression of a PDF's embedded images, and checks each for signs of having been enlarged. An empty result with `unable_to_assess: false` means nothing crossed a threshold, not that the document is clean.

Images edited in after the document was produced: painted over and replaced, stretched or rotated, pasted with a seam, or with altered brightness, colour or noise. An empty result with `unable_to_assess: false` means nothing crossed a threshold, not that the document is clean.

Alignment, margins, spacing and overlaid text. Each finding lists `type`, `page`, `where`, `text`, `summary` and `checks` (detected, expected, difference). An empty result with `unable_to_assess: false` means nothing crossed a threshold, not that the document is clean.
Rules over the file metadata captured at ingestion (author, creator, producer, dates, software); some apply only to institution-issued document types.
The per-type arithmetic and consistency checks on the extracted fields (no file download). One LLM call binds each check's inputs.

post.description:
Re-launches detection after a previous attempt was cancelled or
crashed. NOT a general "run detection" trigger — that only ever
happens automatically on approval (routers/documents.py's
approve_document) — so this is only allowed when the last attempt left
an error/cancellation behind and produced no report, and only when
nothing is already running for this document.

Readiness check: does a real query against Supabase succeed right now?
Suitable for a Cloud Run readiness probe once deployed there — a failure
here should stop new traffic being routed to this instance, not restart
it (the underlying cause is almost never fixed by a restart).
Liveness only — does not touch the database. See /health/db for that.

post.description:
Mints a short-lived, single-use ticket for the case status WebSocket
below. Sits behind require_auth like every other protected endpoint
(this router is registered outside main.py's `_protected` group only
because the WebSocket route itself can't use header-based auth — this
plain HTTP route has no such restriction). See auth.py's
WS_TICKET_TTL_SECONDS docstring for why this exists instead of just
putting the normal bearer token in the WS URL.
